paragraphs: Friend, here is what this passage teaches me. Death runs down that whole family line like a drumbeat, "and then he died," over and over (Genesis 5:5, 8, 11). Then God steps in with one man who breaks the pattern: "Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away" (Genesis 5:24). Nobody else in that list gets a line like that, and I think the Bible wants us to notice who it's about, the man who walked with God.

Then the story turns heavy, and I think this one hurts. The LORD saw that "every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time," and He "was grieved in His heart" (Genesis 6:5-6). Sin is not a small thing, and God does not shrug at it. But look at what grief tells you. The LORD is not cold about this. He cares about what He made, and that matters to every baker reading it.

And then comes the line I want you to carry out of the bakery: "Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD" (Genesis 6:8). Noah's father had hoped this son would bring comfort in the middle of a cursed, tiring world (Genesis 5:29). In the middle of all that dark, one man stands in God's favor. The story isn't over, friend, so keep your oven mitts on.
